title: AI查出数学最大证明的34个错
title_en: AI Found 34 Cracks in Math's Biggest Proof

segments.zh: Fifteen thousand pages.
That's one math proof, and almost nobody has read all of it.
segments.en: 这是一个数学证明，几乎没人把它从头读到尾。

segments.zh: This week, an AI startup called Axiom says its AI agents checked every line.
segments.en: 这周，一家叫Axiom的AI公司说，它的AI把每一行都查了一遍，

segments.zh: In twenty four days.
And it found thirty four real mistakes.
One of them needed brand new math to fix.
segments.en: 其中一个得靠全新的数学才补得上。

segments.zh: Today's brain teaser:
how do you check a proof too big for any human to read?
segments.en: 一个大到没人读得完的证明，怎么检查？

segments.zh: First, what was being proved?
It's called the classification of finite simple groups.
A group is just a set of moves you can combine,
like all the ways to twist a puzzle cube.
segments.en: 比如拧魔方的各种转法。

segments.zh: Simple groups are the building blocks,
the way prime numbers build every other number.
segments.en: 就像质数能拼出所有的数。

segments.zh: The theorem says: here is the complete list of blocks.
segments.en: 这个定理说：积木块的完整清单就在这，

segments.zh: Nothing is missing.
The list has a few infinite families,
segments.en: 清单里有几大无穷家族，

segments.zh: plus twenty six weird loners called sporadic groups.
segments.en: 外加26个怪家伙，叫“散在群”。

segments.zh: The biggest loner is called the Monster.
It has about eight times ten to the fifty three elements.
segments.en: 大约有8乘10的53次方个元素。

segments.zh: That's more than the number of atoms
in the entire Earth.
Proving the list took about a hundred mathematicians
segments.en: 证完这张清单，用了大约一百位数学家，

segments.zh: and more than five hundred papers.
It started in the nineteen fifties.
People announced it was done in nineteen eighty three.
Twist one: it wasn't done.
One gap stayed open until two thousand and four.
segments.en: 有个缺口一直到2004年才补上。

segments.zh: So how do you check fifteen thousand pages?
Stop trusting. Start checking every single step.
Axiom rewrote the proof in a language called Lean.
segments.en: Axiom把证明翻译成一种叫Lean的语言，

segments.zh: Lean is a super picky referee.
Every step has to follow from the steps before it,
segments.en: 每一步都必须从前面推出来，

segments.zh: or Lean flat out says no.
It's like dominoes:
if one domino is missing, the whole chain stops.
Here's the clever part:
the AI writes, and Lean checks.
AI can make things up.
But Lean can't be sweet talked.
Swarms of AI agents wrote about forty three million lines.
segments.en: 一群AI写了大约四千三百万行，

segments.zh: In twenty four days.
Twist two, the surprising one:
the proof people trusted for decades had cracks.
segments.en: 大家信了几十年的证明，有裂缝。

segments.zh: Thirty four errors needed real repair.
Most were typos, mislabeled tables, and missing assumptions.
segments.en: 大多是笔误、表格标错、漏了条件。

segments.zh: But one, deep inside a piece called the Unbalanced Group Theorem,
segments.en: 但有一个，藏在“非平衡群定理”里，

segments.zh: could not be fixed with a quick patch.
Axiom called in two of the original authors, Richard Lyons and Ronald Solomon,
segments.en: Axiom请来当年的两位作者，莱昂斯和所罗门，

segments.zh: and they found a way around it.
That fix is now a new result of its own.
segments.en: 这个补丁成了一个新结果，

segments.zh: And the list of building blocks still stands.
Twist three:
this might be how we check robots, too.
segments.en: 将来查机器人，可能也靠这个。

segments.zh: A self driving car or a surgical robot runs millions of lines of code.
segments.en: 自动驾驶、手术机器人跑着几百万行代码，

segments.zh: Testing can never try every case.
segments.en: 测试不可能试遍所有情况。

segments.zh: In principle, a checker like Lean can prove a rule always holds,
segments.en: 原理上，像Lean这样的检查器能证明一条规矩永远成立，

segments.zh: like this arm never swings into that wall.
segments.en: 比如机械臂永远不撞墙。

segments.zh: Fine print: this is Axiom's own announcement.
segments.en: 友情提示：这是Axiom自己宣布的，

segments.zh: Mathematicians are still going through it.
And Lean only checks the question you wrote.
Write the question wrong, and you prove the wrong thing.
segments.en: 问题写错了，证出来的也是错的东西。

segments.zh: So how do you check a proof nobody can read?
segments.en: 所以，没人读得完的证明怎么查？

segments.zh: Cut every step small enough for a computer to check.
segments.en: 把每一步切到小得电脑能查。

segments.zh: Fifteen thousand pages,
turned into forty three million tiny dominoes.
segments.en: 变成四千三百万块小骨牌。

segments.zh: The tallest stack of paper in math history
segments.en: 数学史上最高的那摞纸，

segments.zh: finally got a second reader.
It just
wasn't a human.
